events.summary: STORY: Unionized workers at South Korea's Kakao staged a four-hour strike and rally on Wednesday.They demanded job security and changes to the tech firm's bonus system. Hundreds of workers wearing black T-shirts and holding white umbrellas walked out of Kakao's office in the morning.The union had told police as many as 1,200 members would join the rally.Local media reported the union plans a general strike for June 29 with all 5,000 members due to take part.Kakao operates South Korea's biggest messaging app by users, and employs about 6,000 people.The dispute comes with growing labor unrest in South Korea as tech firms score record earnings during the global AI boom.Samsung Electronics' union got ⁠a ​deal this month tying chip division bonuses to ​10.5% of operating profit.Kakao said last month it had failed to reach a wage deal with the union in government-mediated talks.The union wants reform to Kakao's compensation system.They argue executives have received higher bonus payments in recent years while other employees have seen limited benefits.Kakao previously said it turned down a union demand for profit-sharing, calling it unrealistic.The union refused to confirm details on the negotiation.Kakao said Wednesday its running a real-time system in response to the strike.It added management will keep talking with the union.

events.summary: South Korea's Kakao Corp union said on Monday it will stage a four-hour strike ‌and rally in Pangyo on June 10, demanding job ‌security and reforms to a compensation system it says disproportionately rewards executives.  In a ​statement, the union said its core demands include halting restructuring such as divestments and spin-offs and improving what it called an "executive-centric pay system" that fuels job insecurity.  The move ⁠comes after government-mediated wage talks broke down last week, with Kakao rejecting union demands — including profit-sharing proposals — as unrealistic and "a big ​burden" on ​management as it prioritises investment ​and shareholder returns.

events.summary: RXO's proprietary Curve truckload market forecast indicates a significant increase in spot rates, marking the biggest sequential rise since 2021. The second quarter saw a 32.4% year-over-year increase, driven by tightening carrier capacity due to federal regulations, which has led to a supply imbalance relative to shipper demand. This trend is expected to continue into peak season, putting increased strain on shippers despite muted overall freight volumes.
events.title: RXO’s Latest Curve Freight Market Forecast Shows the Biggest Sequential Increase in Truckload Spot Rates Since 2021

events.summary: AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE:AU) gained significant attention as gold rallied, with bullion reaching multi-month highs and gold miners experiencing one of their strongest weeks in years. The company, a global gold producer, benefits from easing interest rate expectations and a softening central bank tone, which historically boost precious metals. Its broad global footprint and focus on disciplined cost management position it well to leverage the amplified gains seen by mining companies during gold rallies.
events.title: AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE:AU) Shines As Bullion Nears Multi-Month Highs

events.summary: Shares of RXO, ArcBest, and Lucid plummeted after trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada broke down, leading to concerns about new tariffs and retaliatory measures. The breakdown in talks triggered 50% tariffs on Canadian imports and planned tariffs on vehicles and auto parts, causing investors to pull back from trade-sensitive equities. The article also notes RXO's recent volatility and its performance since its IPO, juxtaposing current dips with past gains driven by different economic news.
events.title: RXO, ArcBest, and Lucid Shares Plummet, What You Need To Know

events.summary: Morgan Stanley has significantly increased its Brent crude forecasts, anticipating a peak of $100 in Q4 2026 due to a slower-than-expected recovery in Middle East supply and tightening market conditions. The bank's strategist, Mike Wilson, also identified a renewed oil spike as the biggest risk to US stocks, recommending energy shares as a portfolio hedge. The upgraded outlook reflects falling oil inventories and a wide gap between crude and refined product prices, indicating constrained refining capacity.
events.title: ICYMI - Morgan Stanley lifts Brent forecast to $100 as oil market tightens

events.summary: Post Holdings (POST) stock presents a valuation-versus-execution dilemma for investors, with its inexpensive valuation and strong Foodservice segment growth contending with weak retail volumes and rising costs. Despite an attractive forward P/E ratio and significant share price drop, the company faces headwinds in its Post Consumer Brands division due to declining volumes and inflation. While robust cash flow allows for capital discipline, the Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) suggests a patient approach is warranted given the mixed growth and value signals.
events.title: Post Holdings Stock: Buy, Hold or Wait as Growth Meets Value

events.summary: Despite the US national debt crossing $40 trillion, household net worth has increased by more than twice that amount over the same period, providing crucial context. While higher interest rates and other concerns persist, strong corporate earnings and the potential for long-term productivity gains from AI suggest that these fears should not overshadow a positive market outlook. Investors are advised to focus on underlying fundamentals like earnings rather than short-term anxieties.
events.title: Don’t let debt fears derail market perspective

events.summary: Morgan Stanley is cautioning investors that bond yields may continue to rise, citing a shift in economic cycles that resembles the post-World War II era. The investment bank believes market dynamics have moved away from the disinflationary period observed from 1982 to 2020. This prediction was initially made by Morgan Stanley in 2021, suggesting a sustained change in economic conditions.
events.title: Morgan Stanley warns bond yields could rise in post-WWII-style era

events.title: FX Weekly Overview (Brazil Issue)

Despite this, gold's momentum is tempered by bond activity, with the long-term outlook dependent on geopolitics and financial management.
events.title: Precious Metals StoneX Bullion weekly round-up; bond yields, debasement; conflicting influences on gold

events.summary: Citigroup and Axis Bank have partnered to finance Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) investing in foreign-currency deposits, utilizing RBI rules for standby letters of credit. events.summary: STORY: U.S. stocks closed higher on Tuesday, with the Dow and S&P 500 each adding nearly a third of a percent, and the Nasdaq climbing two-thirds of a percent.The gains could ease investor concerns sparked by a recent bond market rout that lifted yields and pressured equities. Keith Buchanan is senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments."The market, as we see it from our firm, is just grappling with, what does this newer framework of higher yields, particularly along the Treasury curve, really means for risk assets across the board? We're coming to, you know, a lot of our work is honed in on this, this one metric and this one price, if you will, across risk assets for some time. Seems like the market is finally starting to grapple with, what does that mean as far as discounted cash flows and how you price the risk of the risk landscape? And that process can be churning and frankly could introduce downside volatility. And that's one concern we have is how that really filters through, how folks like myself that sit in our seats look at the world and how we price risk going forward."Longer-dated Treasury yields fell on Tuesday as oil prices dropped to a one-week low and traders continued to weigh the implications of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision to expand Treasury buybacks.:: NvidiaMeanwhile, investors are looking ahead to Nvidia's results on Wednesday as the next test for the earnings-driven rally. Shares of the AI chip giant closed more than 2% higher.Elsewhere in the market, shares of Dick's Sporting Goods plunged 30% after the retailer cut its annual forecasts. And shares of Target fell almost 4% after the retailer apologized for and pulled a Halloween costume criticized for evoking blackface, renewing concerns about brand missteps just as its financial turnaround effort had begun to gain traction.On the economic data front, Wednesday brings updated inflation figures for July, just one day ahead of the start of the Federal Reserve's annual Jackson Hole symposium.
